newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in moderate trade on Thursday with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. June non-farm payrolls report and weekly jobless claims data, dealers said.
The U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to keep short-term interest rates unchanged had little impact on the market, they said.
Non-farm payrolls for June are forecast to be around 222,000 compared with 138,000 reported in May.
The unemployment rate is expected to be unchanged from May's 4.8 percent.
Weekly jobless claims for the week ended June 28, are expected to rise to 336,000 against the previous week's 332,000.

"Rates were steady to easier in the morning on some position adjustments. Some people are waiting for tonight's release of the non-farm payrolls report and weekly jobless claims numbers, for more clues to market direction," a local dealer said.

"The numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared their positions for the day, so I don't think there will be much impact unless the figures are way off market expectations," he said.
In short dates, Thursday/Friday slipped 1/8 percentage point to 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent and weekend eased 1/16 point to 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.
Week-fixed was unchanged from Wednesday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent.

Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8 percent, four-months eased 1/16 point to 5-3/4 5-5/8, six-months eased 1/16 point to 5-7/8 5-3/4 and twelve-months eased 1/16 point to 6-1/16 5-15/16 percent.
